notes: This is the shop's product database. Edit this file to change what the shop sells. 'shop' holds the shop's name and how orders reach you: put your WhatsApp number (with country code, e.g. 6591234567) in 'whatsapp' and/or an address in 'email' to turn the Checkout button into 'send my order'; leave both empty and the shop stays a demo. 'supabase_url' and 'supabase_key' connect the shop to its live stock database (the key is the public 'publishable' one, safe to show here; never put a 'secret' or 'service_role' key in this file); remove them and the shop uses inventory.json instead. Each product has: id (keep it unique and unchanged, the cart uses it), name, category (which shelf it goes on; the order of the 'categories' list sets the shelf order), price_sgd, pack, model (the 3D pack: type 'box' or 'cylinder', width, height, depth in shop units, colour, and optionally 'shape' - one of bag, box, bar, carton, can, tube, cup - if the shop guesses the wrong one from the pack text), and texture. If texture.image_url is set, that photo is used on the pack; otherwise, or if the photo fails to load, the shop draws pack art from the name and colour. Prices are starting shop prices: 'reference.note' says whether each came from a store listing or is an estimate. Change price_sgd to your own selling price before selling. The room grows extra aisles automatically when there are more categories or products. The shop page is virtual-snack-shop.html; keep products.json next to it. After editing this file, run 'python sync-products.py' to check it for mistakes and refresh the backup copy inside the page (used only when the page is opened straight from a file).
